Oregon

25 directory entries · Research in progress

  • Alsea↗Continuing constituent community government association
    Connection & source
    Continuing constituent community government association

    Actual Siletz tribal heritage introduction names Alsea, Coos and Galice/Applegate among distinct constituent peoples; government address is Siletz, Oregon. This is a diaspora/government connection, not all ancestral lands.

    Historical and continuing; geography passage inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Cayuse↗Historical homeland described by the constituent tribal government
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland described by the constituent tribal government

    In its account of the lower Columbia peoples, CTUIR locates Cayuse communities along Blue Mountain tributary valleys and quotes a historical description placing most of their country in Oregon, with a smaller part in Washington Territory. This supports an Oregon historical connection; it does not confine Cayuse history to Oregon.

    Historical homeland before and during nineteenth-century territorial change. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Clackamas↗Historical village and continuing ancestral place connection
    Connection & source
    Historical village and continuing ancestral place connection

    Grand Ronde places its Willamette Falls property on the east bank of the Willamette River in Oregon City. It identifies the former Kosh-huk-shix village there as a Clackamas community and describes treaty cession and forced removal to Grand Ronde. This directly supports an Oregon historical-place connection.

    Village history before the 1855 treaty and forced removal; later Grand Ronde account of ancestral connection. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Clatskanie↗Historical village region connection in specialist scholarship
    Connection & source
    Historical village region connection in specialist scholarship

    Boyd and Zenk explicitly place non-Chinookan Clatskanie villages in present-day Columbia County in the Portland Basin. The named county supplies the Oregon state connection. Their separate treatment of these communities avoids confusing Clatskanie with Chinookan villages or with Clatsop.

    Early nineteenth-century villages in the Portland Basin. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

  • Kathlamet↗Ancestral constituent people geography in the Nation's self description
    Connection & source
    Ancestral constituent people geography in the Nation's self description

    The Nation explicitly identifies Cathlamet (Kathlamet) as a constituent people of present-day Oregon. This directly supplies the spelling relationship and an Oregon connection, while preserving the distinction between a constituent people and the shared Chinook Indian Nation government. Inspection limit: indexed original-source text was inspected; the direct page could not be rendered in this review. This is an inspected excerpt, not a full-work content check.

    Ancestral-community identification described in the Nation's public account. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Takelma↗Historical homeland association

  • Tualatin↗Historical villages / displacement connection
    Connection & source
    Historical villages / displacement connection

    Henry Zenk identifies Tualatin as related independent Northern Kalapuya-speaking villages across Tualatin Plains, Wapato Valley and Chehalem/North Yamhill valleys, and describes removal to Grand Ronde in 1856. Inspection: Opening two paragraphs on villages and language; concluding paragraph on removal and descendants. Limits: State-level Oregon connection; not one historic centralized government. Ceremonial material and dated population statements not used.

    Historical villages and 1856 removal; descendant continuity described by a 2024 article. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Walla Walla↗Historical homeland and seasonal use connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland and seasonal use connection

    The CTUIR history's Life cycle and Foods section explicitly places the three constituent peoples, including Walla Walla, primarily in northeastern Oregon and its neighboring cross-border region. Its lower-Columbia account separately identifies Walla Walla river communities and bands. This is a broad historical connection, not presence everywhere in the state or a merged Cayuse/Umatilla/Walla Walla identity. This supplied-study URL was independently read.

    Historical regional life described before the early 1900s; geography passage inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.
